Israel's population density per square mile has been reported differently across sources and time periods, reflecting the conflict due to outdated information. As of 2025, Britannica reports a density of approximately 1,087.8 persons per square mile [d3], while Worldometer reports 1,139 people per square mile [d1][d8]. An older 2023 figure from ABC News, citing U.S. Census data, placed the density at roughly 1,098 people per square mile when Israel's population was about 9.3 million [d7]. An even older 2017 World Bank figure cited by CEIC recorded only about 402.6 people per square kilometer (roughly 1,042 per square mile), reflecting lower population levels at that time [d9]. The most current and credible estimates for 2025 place Israel's national population density in the range of approximately 1,088 to 1,139 people per square mile [d3][d1][d8], with significant variation by district — for example, the Tel Aviv District reaches as high as 22,693 people per square mile [d4].
